llm.summary: The skill matches its launch-monitoring purpose, but its default screenshot stage opens third-party pages in an unsandboxed browser and writes persistent captures, so users should review it before installing.

dimensions.detail: The script makes outbound requests to built-in or user-supplied feeds, Brave or DuckDuckGo search, and then opens up to 10 result URLs in a browser without a domain allowlist.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no separate auto-install hook, but runtime execution may invoke npx --yes playwright as a fallback, which can fetch and run external tooling.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The quick start runs all stages by default, including external search and screenshots; screenshots can be disabled with --no-screenshots, but the default behavior is fairly broad.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script writes JSON results, markdown reports, and PNG screenshots to disk, and its Chromium path uses --no-sandbox without an isolated browser profile in the command.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: RSS collection, web search, screenshot capture, and report generation are coherent with AI product launch monitoring and are described in the skill documentation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the skill contacting external feeds and search providers and opening discovered URLs in a headless browser. Use --no-screenshots for sensitive environments, avoid internal or authenticated feed URLs, and prefer running it in an isolated workspace or container.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Shell execution, network access, and file writes are central to the documented one-command monitoring pipeline, but the artifact has no machine-readable permission declaration.
[SQP-2] expected: External RSS and search requests are expected and mostly disclosed, but users should understand that custom queries and feed URLs are sent to third-party services.
[SQP-2] expected: Screenshot capture is a documented feature, but the default browser stage opens third-party pages, stores captures, and weakens browser containment with --no-sandbox.
